This step describes how to deliver virally-encoded transgenes intraventricularly into the post-natal day 0 (P0) mouse brain. We used AAV2/6-CaMKIIα-Cre-ERT2 and AAV2/8-hDlx-Cre-ERT2 to achieve widespread transduction of excitatory and inhibitory neurons in Adamtsl3flox/flox mice respectively.1.Transfer the cage containing the mother and pups to a quiet room suitable for injection.a.Place a warming pad under ½ cage to keep the pups warm before injection.b.Cover the remaining ½ with dry task wipes (serves to warm up the pups after injection).c.Remove the mother from the cage and place her in a new, clean cage.d.Count the number of pups born and prepare aliquots of each AVV (AAV2/8-hDlx-Cre-ERT2, and AAV2/6-CaMKIIα-Cre-ERT2).e.Plan to inject 2 μL of AAV for 1 pup (1 μL per ventricle).f.Keep aliquots on ice until ready for injection.Note: Avoid additional freeze-thaw cycles of AAVs to conserve transduction efficacy.Caution: A viral titer between 5.0 × 1012 vg/mL and 1.0 × 1013 vg/mL with an injection volume of 1 μL per ventricle is typically sufficient. steps.title: Breed mice for neonatal injection
steps.instruction: Set up breeding pairs of two female mice with one male mouse, perform at least two simultaneous bleedings, check for a vaginal plug one day after mating, and place pregnant females into a clean cage three days before expected delivery (≈19 ± 1 days after plug). Deliver pups and perform intraventricular AAV injection within 12 h of birth (post‑natal day 0, P0).

steps.title: Prepare AAV aliquots and injection supplies
steps.instruction: Thaw AAV2/6‑CaMKIIα‑Cre‑ERT2 and AAV2/8‑hDlx‑Cre‑ERT2 stocks, keep on ice and avoid additional freeze‑thaw cycles. Prepare 5 × 500 µL aliquots of sterile distilled water for syringe washing. Rinse a 10 µL Hamilton syringe with a 32 G needle five times in each water aliquot. Load 2 µL of each AAV (titer 5.0 × 10¹²–1.0 × 10¹³ vg/mL) into the syringe when needed. Prepare a warming pad, dry task wipes, an ice bucket with an inverted petri dish, and additional dry task wipes for the cold injection stage.

steps.title: Neonatal intraventricular injection of AAV
steps.instruction: Inject 2 µL total AAV per pup (1 µL per ventricle) at P0 using hypothermia anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the dam and litter to a quiet room and place a warming pad under half of the cage; cover the other half with dry task wipes to keep pups warm after injection.
Remove the dam, count pups, and keep AAV aliquots on ice.
Place a dry task‑wipe‑covered inverted petri dish on ice; this will serve as the cold injection stage.
Induce hypothermia anesthesia by transferring one pup onto the cold stage, wait 2–3 min until the pup is immobile, and confirm by gently squeezing a paw (body temperature ≈10 °C).
Wipe the pup’s head with a cotton swab soaked in 70 % ethanol.
Stabilize the pup on the task wipe, head up, and locate the injection site 1 mm lateral to the sagittal suture between lambda and bregma (visible through skin).

Insert the needle perpendicular to the skull to a depth of ~3 mm, inject 1 µL of AAV slowly, then withdraw the needle slowly. Repeat on the contralateral ventricle using the same parameters. Do not exceed 2 µL per ventricle.
Return the pup to the warming pad, wait until it moves normally, then place it back with the litter.
Rinse the Hamilton syringe five times in each of the five water aliquots before switching to the next AAV.
After all pups have received AAV2/6‑CaMKIIα‑Cre‑ERT2, repeat the procedure with AAV2/8‑hDlx‑Cre‑ERT2.
Mark each pup with a laboratory pen for later identification.
Return the dam to the cage only after confirming she is attending the pups.
At weaning age, separate mice, ear‑punch, and record which AAV each mouse received.

steps.title: Prepare tamoxifen solution and inject
steps.instruction: Induce Cre‑ERT2 activity at 2 months of age by intraperitoneal injection of tamoxifen dissolved in corn oil.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve tamoxifen to 10 mg/mL in corn oil (1 mg per mouse = 100 µL). Keep the solution at ≤30 °C to accelerate dissolution, store aliquots at –20 °C protected from light, and keep on ice during injections.
Randomly assign half of the mice injected with AAV2/6‑CaMKIIα‑Cre‑ERT2 (and similarly for AAV2/8‑hDlx‑Cre‑ERT2) to receive tamoxifen; the other half receive corn oil alone.
Inject each mouse intraperitoneally with ≤150 µL of the appropriate solution once daily for five consecutive days.
After the final injection, wait a minimum of 2 weeks before proceeding to tissue collection to allow complete Cre recombination.

steps.title: Prepare reagents for ACSF perfusion
steps.instruction: Make all solutions needed for transcardial perfusion and post‑fixation.

substeps.instruction: Thaw 4 % PFA fixative (prepare 15 mL per mouse) and keep on ice.
Prepare 30 % sucrose in PBS (15 mL per mouse) and store at 4 °C.

Prepare ACSF stock (10×): dissolve 73.05 g NaCl (1.25 M), 21.84 g NaHCO₃ (260 mM), 1.73 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O (12.5 mM), and 1.86 g KCl (25 mM) in distilled water and bring to 1000 mL. Store at 4 °C up to 2 months.

Make 1× ACSF on the day of perfusion: mix 100 mL 10× stock, 4.5 g glucose (25 mM), 2 mL 1 M CaCl₂ (2.5 mM), 2 mL 1 M MgCl₂ (2 mM), and bring to 1000 mL with distilled water. Bubble with carbogen (95 % O₂/5 % CO₂) for ≥30 min on ice, adjust pH to 7.4 if needed, and keep oxygenated on ice.

Prepare 0.4 M Na‑phosphate buffer (1000 mL): dissolve 46 g Na₂HPO₄ (324 mM) and 10.5 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O (76 mM) in ~900 mL water, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 M NaOH or HCl, then bring to 1000 mL. Store at room temperature up to 6 months.

steps.title: Transcardial perfusion with ACSF
steps.instruction: Perfuse each mouse with oxygenated ACSF followed by brief post‑fixation.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the mouse and anesthetize with an intraperitoneal overdose of pentobarbital (≈50 mg/kg). Confirm deep anesthesia by pinching tail and paws.
Pin the animal on a cork board, open the thorax, and expose the heart.
Insert a 15‑gauge needle through the left ventricle into the ascending aorta, following the heart axis, and cut the right atrium with a hook to allow outflow.
Start a peristaltic pump at ≤16 mL/min and perfuse oxygenated ACSF. Perfusion is complete when the liver turns beige‑yellow (usually <2 min). Stop the pump.
Remove the mouse, decapitate, and extract the brain with forceps. Cut the brain into 2–3 pieces appropriate for the region of interest.
Place brain pieces into a 15 mL tube containing 15 mL 4 % PFA and post‑fix for 90–120 min at room temperature.
Rinse brains in cold PBS, then transfer to 15 mL of 30 % sucrose in PBS at 4 °C. Keep until the tissue sinks (usually overnight).

steps.title: Section brains on sliding microtome
steps.instruction: Obtain 40 µm free‑floating sections from cryoprotected brains.

substeps.instruction: Mount a fresh blade in a Microm HM 400 R sliding microtome (or equivalent).
Start the freezing stage, apply a drop of tissue‑mounting fluid, let it almost freeze, straighten with a razor blade, and place the brain in the mounting fluid in the desired orientation.
Freeze the mounting fluid completely.
Set the microtome to cut at 40 µm thickness.
Collect sections one by one with a wet brush into a multi‑well plastic box filled with cold PBS placed on ice (dark background).
Store sections at 4 °C in PBS for up to 24 h, or transfer to anti‑freeze solution (≈800 mL) in a sealed container and store at –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Prepare immunofluorescence solutions
steps.instruction: Make Tris‑Triton wash buffer, primary/secondary antibody diluents, and anti‑freeze storage solution.

substeps.instruction: Tris‑Triton (pH 7.4, 1 L): dissolve 60.6 g Tris (0.5 M) and 87.7 g NaCl (1.5 M) in ~900 mL water, add 5 mL 10 % Triton X‑100 stock to reach 0.05 % final, adjust pH to 7.4 with HCl, bring to 1 L, and store at room temperature.

Anti‑freeze solution (≈800 mL): mix 62.5 mL 0.4 M Na‑phosphate buffer (31.25 mM), 150 g glucose (1 M), 300 mL ethylene glycol, 200 mg sodium azide (3.8 mM), and 437.5 mL distilled water; store at 4 °C up to 3 months (sections stored at –20 °C).
Primary antibody mix (in Tris‑Triton with 2 % serum of the same species as secondary):
Rabbit anti‑GABA_AR α2 (1:2000),
Guinea‑pig anti‑GABA_AR γ2 (1:2000),
Mouse anti‑Gephyrin (1:1000).
Secondary antibody mix (in Tris‑Triton with 2 % serum):
Donkey anti‑Mouse Cy3 (1:500),
Donkey anti‑Guinea‑pig Alexa 647 (1:500),
Donkey anti‑Mouse Alexa 488 (1:500).

steps.title: Immunofluorescence labeling of free‑floating sections
steps.instruction: Label brain sections with primary and secondary antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Place sections (≤5–6 per well) into a 12‑well plate filled with Tris‑Triton buffer.
Wash sections 3 × 10 min on a shaker at 50–100 rpm, moving sections to a new well for each wash.
Aliquot 500 µL of primary antibody mix into each well of a 9‑well glass plate; add sections and incubate in a moist chamber with continuous agitation (≈100 rpm) overnight at 4 °C.
After primary incubation, wash sections again 3 × 10 min in fresh Tris‑Triton (same shaker conditions).
Aliquot 500 µL of secondary antibody mix into each well of a new 9‑well glass plate; add sections and incubate in a moist chamber with agitation (≈100 rpm) for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash sections a final 3 × 10 min in Tris‑Triton.
Mount sections on gelatin‑coated slides, allow to air‑dry, then coverslip with Dako fluorescence mounting medium.
Let the mounting medium polymerize overnight (≥12 h) and store slides at 4 °C in a closed slide carton.

steps.title: Acquire images on Airyscan microscope
steps.instruction: Capture high‑resolution images of stained sections for synaptic puncta analysis.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the CLSM 900 Airyscan system and allow it to reach a stable temperature; perform all manufacturer‑recommended calibrations.
Remove a slide, let it equilibrate to room temperature for a few minutes, and clean the coverslip surface.
Using a low‑magnification objective and a ubiquitous marker (e.g., DAPI or NeuN), locate the hippocampal CA1 region.
Switch to a 63× oil‑immersion objective. Do not excite the synaptic fluorophores while locating the region to avoid photobleaching.

Set acquisition parameters: pixel size 35 nm, optical section thickness 260 nm, Z‑stack of 5 sections with 130 nm step size (total depth ≈0.65 µm), 2× scan average, pixel dwell time 0.52 µs, and ensure no channel bleed‑through.
For Airyscan processing, keep the Z‑stack depth ≤1 µm (minimum 5 optical sections) and enable the 3D‑processing option.
Adjust laser intensity and detector gain for each channel individually; avoid saturated pixels.
Acquire 6–10 images per brain section (or more as needed) to assess variability, keeping all settings identical across all sections and animals.
Save images in the appropriate format for downstream analysis.
